findings.summary: Bounded Texas discovery screened five candidates and added no route because each failed a hard gate before implementation.
details: Whitewater Sports-to-Rio Guadalupe and Rio Guadalupe-to-Mountain Breeze remain blocked by stale TPWD leased-access periods from 2017-2018.
Blanco FM 179-to-FM 1492 remains blocked by unresolved FM 1492 public take-out, parking, coordinate, camping, and safety evidence.
Nueces CR 390-to-CR 414 has route, threshold, and live same-river gauge support, but lacks manager-grade endpoint coordinates/access and official camping legality.
SASPAMCO Helton-to-Floresville remains blocked by SARA downstream-of-Helton closure for large log jams.

findings: The 2026-08-11 08:00 UTC bounded Texas pass continued past blockers and added elm-fork-trinity-river-california-crossing-frasier-dam as a 5.5-mile direct-USGS Elm Fork Trinity National Water Trail segment with Trinity Coalition endpoint coordinates and route shape, TRPA 100 / 200-1,000 / 2,000 cfs guidance, USGS 08055500 product-live flow at 105 cfs / 3.46 ft, no route camping under Dallas park rules, mandatory Frasier Dam take-out and urban/dam/strainer/private-bank safety notes, generated geometry, put-in ok and take-out review coordinate results, expected upstream shared-endpoint overlap only, and a bounded no-image row.

The same 2026-08-11 pass first blocked tx-devils-bakers-crossing-san-pedro because the same-river USGS Devils River gauge candidates 08449000 and 08449400 lacked current product-supported discharge/stage data; live Dolan Creek tributary data was rejected as a route gauge substitute.

The same 2026-08-11 pass then blocked tx-trinity-east-fork-us80-i20 because the selected East Fork Trinity lead lacked a manager-backed public endpoint/camping package, while the Forney gauge was stale and the live Crandall gauge did not cure the route-package gap.

The 2026-08-11 06:08 UTC bounded Texas pass added no route after screening five candidates: Staples-Dam-to-River-Grove is blocked by TPWD River Grove temporary closure; Middle Brazos Hwy67-to-Brazos Point still has TRPA thresholds and product-live USGS 08091000 but lacks a fresh manager-backed public endpoint/camping package; Riverside-Park-to-Spivey-Crossing has TPWD route/access/safety and product-live USGS 08093100 at 53.9 cfs / 6.08 ft but lacks durable numeric thresholds; Pete's-Pecan-Patch-to-Grobe-or-Yate's has an active TPWD put-in but lacks downstream public take-out legality/coordinates/camping limits; County-Road-150-to-South-Llano-State-Park is an active TPWD connector but is contained within existing South Llano coverage.

The 2026-08-11 04:08 UTC bounded Texas pass added no route after screening five distinct non-duplicate candidates: Rio Libros-to-Brazos-Outdoor-Center is blocked by TPWD Rio Libros temporary closure; Staples-Dam-to-River-Grove is blocked by TPWD River Grove temporary closure; Spivey-Crossing-to-Brazos-River-Nature-Center cleared much of the evidence package but failed implementation-level coordinate audit with TPWD access anchors 2010 ft and 1546 ft from the matched Brazos flowline and no autonomous-safe corrections; Brazos Outdoor Center lacks a selected manager-backed point-to-point route package; WJF/Hidden-Shores Smithville connectors appear duplicate/contained within existing lower-Colorado coverage without a distinct route package.
